content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1, the no-cost rebalance: it lifts the 14:30-16:30 service level to 89.5% against the 80% target at no extra cost.","why":"A sick wave is behind the 12% staffing shortfall. Payments has 11 absences against a usual 2.8, and general has 10 against a usual 2.6. Call volume and handle time are roughly on plan. P1 delays payments breaks from 14:30-15:00 by 45 minutes, moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments between 14:30 and 15:30, and offers IVR callback on payments from 15:00 to 15:30. That raises payments from 83.4% to 87.6% and general from 91.4% to 92.1%, for 89.5% overall. Abandons fall from 2.2% to 1.5% and the rest-of-day figure rises to 94.7%. It costs INR 0, follows policy, and is the cheapest plan that clearly beats the target.","trade_offs":["Doing nothing (P0) already predicts 86.8%, above target, but payments sits at only 83.4%, which leaves little buffer if more agents go home. P1 adds margin for free.","P4 (demand-side relief) costs INR 264 and gives 95.2%, with 94.2% on payments and 0.5% abandons. That is noticeably better customer impact for a small cost and is worth considering if you want more headroom.","P2 (INR 720, 92.7%) and P3 (INR 1,344, 94.7%, 0.4% abandons) cost more and do not beat P4 on service level.","Moving 3 agents out of general carries a small risk to that queue, but general is still predicted at 92.1%, higher than under no action."],"watch":"Watch payments service level closely from 14:30 to 15:30. If it drops toward 80% or more absences come in, step up to P4's chat deflection or P2's overtime. Also confirm general holds above target while the 3 agents are moved. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
